findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
findings.body: `StatefulDetectorHandler` (src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:135-170) declares four abstract members: `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values` and the new `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. The class body here is just `pass`, so none are implemented. `MetricAlertFire.detector_handler` (line 27) points at this class, and `Detector.detector_handler` (src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py:86) calls `group_type.detector_handler(self)`. For a detector of type `metric_alert_fire` that call now raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class`, so `process_detectors` raises as well. Before this change the handler's `evaluate` returned `[]`. Either implement the four members (stubs that return empty values would do) or keep the previous no-op `DetectorHandler` until the stateful version is built. The `# TODO: This will be a stateful detector...` comment on line 10 is also stale now.

findings.title: Expected occurrence is built with a different value than the one evaluated
findings.body: In `test_results_on_change` the packet value is 100 but the expected occurrence is built with value 6. In `test_dedupe` the packet value is 8 and the expectation uses 6. `test_state_results_multi_group` evaluates group_2 with 10 and builds its expectation with 6. The tests pass only because `MockDetectorStateHandler.build_occurrence_and_event_data` ignores `value`. If the mock ever uses `value`, these tests fail for no real reason. They also do not check that `value` is forwarded to `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Use the real value in the expectations, or have the mock put `value` into `evidence_data` so the tests check it.

findings.title: Duplicate group-key handling is no longer tested and has no replacement
findings.body: `process_detectors` used to log an error for duplicate group keys, and the test for that was deleted. Results are now a dict, so duplicates cannot reach it. A handler that returns two results for one key would simply overwrite one, but `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` builds the dict from `group_values.items()`, which has unique keys, so this is safe there. Custom `DetectorHandler.evaluate` implementations are now bound by the dict return type. Nothing here needs fixing, but the removed error log is a silent behaviour change.
